deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a library loan request slip (Bestellzettel), probably for the Göttingen University Library, written and signed by Riemann.

The ink text reads: 'Poggendorff. Annalen der Physik und Chemie. 3 Reihe Bd 11. 1847. nebst Tafeln zu [crossed out: Bd. 10-12] 3 Reihe Bd 10-12'. It is signed 'B Riemann, Dr. ph.' with his address in parentheses, 'Barfüßerstr. ...'. The last word is probably the householder's name and is not securely legible.

Other markings:
- A red date, 'Oct. 30. 54.', i.e. 30 October 1854. This is probably the library's date of issue or return.
- A large pencil '84', which is likely a slip or sequence number.
- A pencil '0. 71 W.' at the top, which looks like a librarian's shelf note.
- An archival pencil label 'Riemann 2' and the folio number '29'.

The volume numbering works out as follows. Poggendorff's Annalen ran in series of 30 volumes:
- 1st series: vols 1-30 (1824-33)
- 2nd series: vols 31-60
- 3rd series: vols 61-90 (1844-53)

So '3. Reihe Bd 11' is overall vol 71 (1847), matching both the year 1847 and the pencil '71'. The plates requested for 3. Reihe Bd 10-12 are overall vols 70-72.

Context: the request dates from the autumn after Riemann's Habilitation (June 1854), when he had just become Privatdozent. At that time he was working on electrostatic and electrochemical problems: his 1854 note on the distribution of electric tension in ponderable bodies (related to Kohlrausch's residual-charge experiments) and his 1855 paper on Nobili's colour rings. Borrowing 1840s volumes of the Annalen fits that research. Which specific article in vol 71 he wanted cannot be determined from the slip.

The next page is the mirror-image show-through of a similar slip. Its fractions a/b and (r+p+q)/(v+t+s) are probably jottings or show-through, not part of this folio.

results.what: Library loan request by Riemann for Poggendorff's Annalen der Physik und Chemie, 3rd series vol 11 (= vol 71, 1847) and the plates to 3rd series vols 10-12 (= vols 70-72), dated 30 Oct 1854

deep.surprise_reason: A routine library slip with no mathematical content. It is of minor biographical interest: it documents Riemann reading 1847 physics literature in autumn 1854 and his Göttingen address. That his library borrowings exist and have been studied is known.

checkable.asserts: Annalen 3rd series vol 11 corresponds to overall vol 71 (each series has 30 volumes), consistent with the pencil '71' on the slip
Volumes run roughly three per year, so no simple two-volumes-per-year formula applies; the year 1847 is confirmed directly by the slip rather than computed

transcription_corrections: The pencil marking at top centre, '0. 71 W.' (overall volume number 71, likely a librarian's note), is omitted from the transcription.
'8 [?] 4' is a single large pencil number '84' with a small mark between the digits; it is a slip or sequence number, not mathematics.
The folio number '29' is pencilled at the top right.
In the address, 'Barfüßerstr.' is clear; the following word (transcribed 'Agel') is uncertain and is probably the name of the householder.
